title: Quality improvement, change and sustainable care
blurb: Run a small PDSA test of change with the right measures, advocate for evidence-informed change, know the NHS net zero targets, and share data safely between teams.
question: A midwife wants to increase the number of women who have a carbon monoxide test at 36 weeks. Her team has an idea for a prompt in the antenatal record. What should they do first?

teach.body: SPM 5.1 asks midwives to know quality improvement (QI) methods and actively engage in evidence-informed QI. QI is a systematic way of making care safer, more effective and more personal by testing changes and measuring whether they help. In plain English: instead of guessing or rolling out a big change overnight, you try a small change, measure what happens, learn and try again.
teach.cite: SPM 5.1; NHS England Model for Improvement

head: Question
Gives you
rows: What are we trying to accomplish?
How will we know a change is an improvement?
What change can we make that will result in improvement?
teach.caption: Then test each change idea with Plan, Do, Study, Act cycles.

teach.body: SBL v3 asks for carbon monoxide testing at booking and 36 weeks. Midwife Tola's audit shows 62% tested at 36 weeks. Aim: 90% in three months. She predicts a record prompt will help, tests it with two midwives for one week (Plan, Do), and finds it is missed on busy days (Study). They move the prompt to the 36-week checklist (Act) and run the next cycle, watching clinic times as a balancing measure. Then they re-audit and share the results.
teach.cite: SBL v3.2 element 1; Model for Improvement; HQIP audit cycle

teach.body: SPM 5.11 asks midwives to collaborate in, implement and evaluate evidence-informed change at individual, group and service level; SPM 5.13.4 to advocate for change. That means bringing evidence and local data, involving colleagues and the women who use the service from the start, testing on a small scale and showing results. A-EQUIP's 'personal action for quality improvement' function expects every midwife to contribute, for example through audit, embedding learning from incidents and acting on feedback.

teach.caption: Against a 1990 baseline. SPM 5.10: know the principles and methods of sustainable health care.

teach.h: Sharing data between teams and agencies
teach.body: SPM 5.12 asks midwives to use digital and other technologies responsibly to access, record, share and apply data within teams and between agencies. Use approved, secure systems, record accurately at the time (Code 10), share what is needed with those who need it, and tell the woman why and when information may be shared (CG110 1.1.9). Transfer of care from midwife to health visitor must be clearly communicated (NG194 1.1.9).
teach.cite: SPM 5.12; NMC Code 5, 10; NICE CG110, NG194

teach.text: The S in PDSA is Study, not Check: compare the results with your prediction. And a PDSA test starts small; rolling a change out across the trust before testing is not QI.

items: Model for Improvement: aim, measures, changes, then PDSA cycles.
PDSA: Plan with a prediction, Do on a small scale, Study against the prediction, Act to adopt, adapt or abandon.
Measure outcome, process and balancing effects.
NHS net zero: 2040 for emissions it controls (80% cut by 2028–2032), 2045 for emissions it influences.
Share data through secure, approved systems and tell women why and when information is shared.

summary: You can now plan a PDSA test of change with an aim and the three kinds of measure, and advocate for evidence-informed change with colleagues and women. You can also state the NHS net zero targets and share data responsibly between teams.

A.q: In a PDSA cycle, what does the S stand for?
options: Study
Spread
Standard
Sustain
A.why: PDSA = Plan, Do, Study, Act. Study means analysing the results and comparing them with the prediction.

whyNot.1: Spread happens after successful cycles, not as a PDSA step.
whyNot.2: A standard is used in audit, not a PDSA step.
whyNot.3: Sustaining change follows testing; it is not the S in PDSA.

A.q: A team uses the Model for Improvement to reduce triage delays. Which question do they ask first?
options: Who is responsible for the delays?
What are we trying to accomplish?
How much will the change cost?
Which other units have solved this?
A.why: The Model for Improvement starts with the aim: what are we trying to accomplish? Then measures and change ideas.

whyNot.0: Looking for someone to blame is not part of the model.
whyNot.2: Cost matters, but it is not one of the three questions.
whyNot.3: Learning from others can inform change ideas, but the aim comes first.

A.q: By what year does the NHS aim to reach net zero for the emissions it controls directly?
A.why: Net zero by 2040 for the NHS Carbon Footprint (emissions it controls directly), with an 80% reduction by 2028–2032.

whyNot.0: 2030 falls within the 80% interim reduction window, not the net zero date.
whyNot.1: 2035 is not an NHS net zero target date.
whyNot.2: 2045 is the target for emissions the NHS can influence.

B.q: A team introduces a new rapid triage process to cut waiting times in the maternity assessment unit. Which is a balancing measure?
options: Average time from arrival to triage
Proportion of women triaged by a midwife
Delays to planned inductions on the ward
Women's satisfaction with triage
B.why: A balancing measure checks whether the change causes problems elsewhere in the system, such as staff being pulled from inductions.

whyNot.0: Time to triage is the main process measure.
whyNot.1: This measures how the process is done, a process measure.
whyNot.3: Satisfaction reflects the outcome for women, not an unintended effect elsewhere.

B.q: A midwife has designed a new postnatal discharge checklist. What is the best first step under a PDSA approach?
options: Make the checklist trust policy at once
Ask managers to approve it for all wards
Send it to every midwife by email
Test it with a few women for one week
B.why: PDSA tests change on a small scale first, with a prediction, so problems are found before spreading.

whyNot.0: Making it policy before testing skips the learning stage.
whyNot.1: Approving wide rollout without testing is not a PDSA approach.
whyNot.2: Emailing it out is spread without testing.

B.q: A community midwife is transferring a family's care to the health visitor. Which approach to sharing the information is most appropriate?
options: A secure handover through the approved record system
A photo of the notes sent by personal messaging app
A verbal message left with the GP receptionist
A copy of the notes left at the family's home
B.why: NG194 1.1.9: transfer to the health visitor must be clearly communicated; SPM 5.12 and Code 5 require secure, responsible sharing through approved systems.

whyNot.1: Personal messaging apps are not secure or approved for clinical records.
whyNot.2: An informal message is not clear communication of transfer of care.
whyNot.3: Leaving notes does not inform the health visitor.

C.q: A team's first PDSA cycle shows that a new pre-birth checklist was used for 9 of 10 women, as predicted, with no delays. What should they do next?
options: Stop, as the aim has been achieved
Write a research paper on the result
Adopt or adapt it and test on a larger scale
Return to the Plan stage with a new idea
C.why: Act: adopt or adapt the change and plan the next cycle, often testing under more conditions before spreading and re-auditing.

whyNot.0: One small test does not show sustained improvement across the service.
whyNot.1: QI results are shared locally; a single test is not research.
whyNot.3: The idea worked, so there is no need to abandon it for a new one.

C.q: A midwife reads strong evidence for a change in practice that her unit has not adopted. Which approach best fits SPM 5.11 and 5.13.4?
options: Change her own practice without telling the team
Wait for the next national guideline update
Raise a formal complaint about the unit
Bring the evidence and propose a tested change
C.why: SPM 5.11 and 5.13.4: collaborate in, implement and evaluate evidence-informed change, and advocate for it, for example through a team-supported QI test.

whyNot.0: Acting alone without the team bypasses collaboration and governance.
whyNot.1: Waiting misses the chance to advocate for change.
whyNot.2: A complaint is not the route for an improvement idea.

C.q: A maternity unit wants to improve postnatal care for women who have a caesarean. Which approach best involves the women who use the service?
options: Co-design changes with women who used it
Ask staff what they think women want
Copy the approach used by another unit
Send women the new plan once agreed
C.why: SPM 5.3: work with women, partners and families to develop improvement strategies; NICE CG110 1.1.4 also asks services to involve women and families in determining needs.

whyNot.1: Staff views are useful but do not replace women's own experience.
whyNot.2: Another unit's solution may not meet local women's needs.
whyNot.3: Telling women after decisions is information, not involvement.

reteach.title: Small tests, big learning
reteach.question: Why test a change on a few women before rolling it out?

blocks.body: A small test reveals problems while they are easy to fix: the prompt that gets missed on busy days, the form that takes too long. You predict, try, study and act. Each cycle builds evidence, and the team that tested it owns it. Measures tell you whether care improved, whether the step was done, and whether anything else suffered.

blocks.text: Big-bang rollout is the opposite of a PDSA test.

explain.body: A process measure checks whether the steps you changed are actually happening, such as the percentage of women offered CO testing at 36 weeks.

test.q: In a project to improve CO testing, which is a process measure?
options: Number of babies born small
Women's smoking rate at birth
Percentage tested at 36 weeks
Antenatal clinic running time
test.why: A process measure checks whether the intended step is done: the percentage of women tested.

whyNot.0: Birth weight is an outcome measure.
whyNot.1: Smoking at birth is an outcome measure.
whyNot.3: Clinic running time is a balancing measure.

explain.body: Net zero by 2040 for emissions the NHS controls directly (the NHS Carbon Footprint); net zero by 2045 for emissions it can influence (Carbon Footprint Plus), such as its supply chain.

test.q: By when does the NHS aim to reach net zero for the emissions it can influence, such as its supply chain?
test.why: Net zero by 2045 for the NHS Carbon Footprint Plus, the emissions it can influence.

whyNot.0: 2040 is for emissions the NHS controls directly.
whyNot.2: 2050 is not the NHS target date.
whyNot.3: 2032 is the end of the window for an 80% cut in direct emissions.

explain.body: A-EQUIP's fourth function asks every midwife to contribute to quality improvement: reflecting and teaching others, audit and research, embedding learning from incidents, and acting on user and staff feedback.

test.q: Which activity is an example of a midwife's personal action for quality improvement under A-EQUIP?
options: Attending a mandatory fire safety update
Embedding learning from an incident in practice
Completing her annual leave request
Updating her contact details with the NMC
test.why: A-EQUIP Box 2 lists embedding learning from incidents, participating in audit and research, and acting on feedback as personal action for QI.

whyNot.0: Mandatory training is not in itself a QI contribution.
whyNot.3: Updating registration details is a professional requirement, not QI.

explain.body: Share data through approved secure systems, only what is needed, with those who need it, and keep accurate records. Tell the woman why and when her information may be shared.

test.q: A midwife needs to tell the GP about a woman's postnatal complication. Which method best meets SPM 5.12 and the Code?
options: A message from her personal phone
A note given to the woman to deliver
A summary through the approved electronic system
A conversation in the surgery waiting room
test.why: Approved, secure electronic systems protect confidentiality and create a record (SPM 5.12; Code 5, 10).

whyNot.0: Personal devices are not secure for clinical information.
whyNot.1: Relying on the woman to deliver it is not a reliable handover.
